labels.label: T-abs-locate-extension/0-characterisation

source.statement: Lemma 2.17, proof, case 1 (the first exit s0 := sup{s | gamma([0,s)) in iota(M)})

hypotheses.paper: timelike curves realise the chronological relation (both sources define it by curves)
hypotheses.note: C.CausallyArcConnected, the target's uses entry causally_arc_connected
not used: the characterisation holds for every open O of every topological space

findings: New with respect to both sources, and the sharp form of the lemma: in a causally arc-connected spacetime a future (past) chronal curve leaves the open set O iff I+(O) is not contained in O (I-(O) not contained in O), and some chronal curve leaves O iff some point of the boundary of O is chronologically related to some point (futureBoundary_union_pastBoundary_nonempty_iff). The curve's endpoint lies on the boundary (futureBoundary_subset_frontier), which Sbierski states only as 'not in iota(M)' (sbierski2015c.txt:657).
questions: Reading of GKS's future/past boundary (Def 3.7, grant2018inextendibility.txt:407-413): the points p outside O reached by a future (past) chronal curve gamma of M over [0,1] with gamma([0,1)) in O and gamma(1) = p; for O open this is GKS's 'p in boundary of iota(X)' (proved, not assumed).

labels.label: T-abs-locate-extension/1-locate

source.statement: target T-abs-locate-extension, title (the form to be formalized)
Q2 (locating an extension listed as purely causal or topological) and Q4 #2

hypotheses.paper: (M, g) time-oriented Lorentzian with smooth metric; iota a C^k isometric embedding into a Lorentzian manifold of the same dimension
hypotheses.note: iota : N -> M an open embedding (IsOpenEmbedding) of a non-empty topological space; only the openness of range iota is used. Before its endpoint the curve is a chronal curve of the open set range iota on every [0, s], s < 1 (the ETT shadow of 'iota^-1 o gamma is a timelike curve of M', sbierski2015c.txt:709-710)

hypotheses.paper: iota(M) a proper subset; all manifolds connected (tacit, sbierski2015c.txt:628)
I+(q, U) open (Sbierski Prop 2.6); GKS: I+(q) cap Omega a neighbourhood of p; target title 'with I+ open', uses entry causally_open_future
hypotheses.note: not a hypothesis: the openness of I+_U(x) and I-_U(x) is an axiom of an ETT causality (Causality.isOpen_lt_right/left). causally_open_future (J+_U(V) open for open V) is not used by any proof, and would not help: isolatedLine is causally open in both directions

hypotheses.paper: timelike curves realise the chronological relation (by definition in both sources)
hypotheses.note: C.CausallyArcConnected (exists_leaving); exists_leaving_of_local asks it only of a neighbourhood W of each boundary point

hypotheses.paper: 'Let q in I-(p, U)' (Sbierski, time-oriented neighbourhood, sbierski2015c.txt:661); GKS: I+-(p) cap Omega nonempty (localising neighbourhood, grant2018inextendibility.txt:427)
hypotheses.note: HasChronalNeighbour p for every p in the boundary of O: (I+(p)).Nonempty or (I-(p)).Nonempty, one-sided. Necessary: not_exists_leaving_bare; at one boundary point necessary and sufficient: futureBoundary_union_pastBoundary_nonempty_iff. Supplier, layer 3: C0 time-oriented Lorentzian manifolds, every point, both sides (the coordinate line of a chart in which d/dx0 is timelike, as in the proof of Sbierski Prop 2.6, sbierski2015c.txt:450-466); Lorentzian length spaces, every point of a localising neighbourhood, both sides (Kunzinger-Saemann Def 3.16 (ii), kunzinger2018lorentzian.txt:1296-1299); E>=0-manifolds, the future side (rem:btz_pas_tarentin, ETT.tex:1358; the field SingularFlatAxioms.mem_Zplus of Causal.SingularFlat, with BTZAxioms.Iminus_eq_empty at BTZ points; not imported, layer-1 rule). Under arc-connectedness it is p in Z+ or Z- with no separation (CausallyArcConnected.hasChronalNeighbour_iff).

findings: The target's printed form (programme/roadmap.toml:202: an open proper embedding into a connected, causally arc-connected spacetime with I+ open has a chronal curve leaving the image) is false in ETT. not_exists_leaving_bare: on R, isolatedLine (the timelike line of R minus {0}, with 0 related to itself only) is causally arc-connected, causally open for J+ and J-, and causally plain; O = (0, oo) is a connected, proper, non-empty open set (the image of the inclusion); no chronal curve, future or past, leaves it, because its only boundary point 0 has no chronological future or past. What both Lorentzian proofs take from the metric is a chronological neighbour of the boundary point ('Let q in I-(p, U)', sbierski2015c.txt:661; 'I+-(p) cap Omega nonempty', grant2018inextendibility.txt:427); in ETT it is a hypothesis, and it is exactly what is needed (futureBoundary_union_pastBoundary_nonempty_iff).

'I+ open' costs nothing in ETT, and the target's uses entry causally_open_future is not what Sbierski's Prop 2.6 provides: the openness of I+-(q) for points is an axiom of a causality, while causally_open_future is the openness of J+_U(V) for open V. No proof here uses it.

The pairing in the target's title ('with I+ open' and 'covers BTZ points where I- = empty') does not match the proofs. With only I+ of points open (GKS's case 2, grant2018inextendibility.txt:437-438; Sbierski's case 2, sbierski2015c.txt:669-671) the argument needs q in I-(p), which a BTZ point lacks; covering a BTZ point with q in I+(p) uses the openness of I-(q). ETT has both, so the one-sided point is the chronal neighbour, past or future (label 2-one-sided).

The future alternative alone is false even when every hypothesis holds: timelikeLine_futureBoundary_Ioi ((0, oo) is a chronological future set of the timelike line), while timelikeLine_pastBoundary_Ioi_nonempty. Sbierski's 'without loss of generality future directed (otherwise reverse the time orientation)' (sbierski2015c.txt:710-711) is the passage to C.dual.

Neither source is wrong in its own setting: in a C0 Lorentzian manifold, and in a Lorentzian length space (localising neighbourhoods), every point has a chronological past and future in every neighbourhood.
questions: 'timelike curve' (Sbierski) and 'timelike curve' with gamma([0,1)) in iota(X) (GKS) read as future- or past-directed: stated as C.ChronalCurveOn top gamma 0 1 or C.dual.ChronalCurveOn top gamma 0 1, which is what both proofs produce (case 1 a future curve, case 2 a past one) and what GKS's 'boundary+ union boundary- nonempty' says; for the embedding form, one orientation D in {C, C.dual} is fixed for the whole curve and its restrictions.

'leaving the image' read as Sbierski's gamma([0,1)) in iota(M) and gamma(1) not in iota(M), strengthened to gamma(1) in the boundary of iota(M); 'proper' as range iota != univ; N non-empty (Sbierski's manifolds are tacitly connected, hence non-empty).

Should HasChronalNeighbour become a ladder node (e.g. 'every point has a chronal neighbour', one-sided)? The ladder already names the two-sided local form 'chronal neighbours in every open set' as the side condition of causallyOpen_of_pushUp (programme/ladder.toml:239-247); under arc-connectedness the pointwise one-sided form gives the one-sided local form in every open W containing p (CausallyArcConnectedOn.Iplus_nonempty_of_le).
The target's uses should read [causally_arc_connected] plus the named HasChronalNeighbour; causally_open_future is unused.

labels.label: T-abs-locate-extension/2-one-sided

source.statement: rem:btz_pas_tarentin (every point of an E>=0-manifold is strongly tarentin in the future; BTZ points are not in the past)
Definition 3.16 (ii), the non-triviality condition of localising neighbourhoods

hypotheses.paper: 'Let q in I-(p, U)' (a chronological past of the boundary point in a small neighbourhood)
hypotheses.note: (C.Iplus W {p}).Nonempty alone (exists_leaving_of_Iplus_nonempty), or (C.Iminus W {p}).Nonempty alone; nothing of the other side. Witness that the one-sided hypothesis is genuinely weaker: closedHalfLine_oneSided (the closed half-line [0, oo) with the timelike causality; its endpoint has I- empty and I+ non-empty, and a chronal curve leaves (0, oo)). Supplier, layer 3: C0 time-oriented Lorentzian manifolds, every point, both sides (the coordinate line of a chart in which d/dx0 is timelike, as in the proof of Sbierski Prop 2.6, sbierski2015c.txt:450-466); Lorentzian length spaces, every point of a localising neighbourhood, both sides (Kunzinger-Saemann Def 3.16 (ii), kunzinger2018lorentzian.txt:1296-1299); E>=0-manifolds, the future side (rem:btz_pas_tarentin, ETT.tex:1358; the field SingularFlatAxioms.mem_Zplus of Causal.SingularFlat, with BTZAxioms.Iminus_eq_empty at BTZ points; not imported, layer-1 rule). Under arc-connectedness it is p in Z+ or Z- with no separation (CausallyArcConnected.hasChronalNeighbour_iff).

hypotheses.paper: U a small time-oriented neighbourhood of p; the timelike curves lie in U
hypotheses.note: W any open set, causally arc-connected (CausallyArcConnectedOn W); the curve is a chronal curve of W

hypotheses.paper: E>=0-manifold form: every boundary point strongly tarentin in the future
hypotheses.note: exists_leaving_of_frontier_subset_Zplus: frontier O in Z+(M); supplier rem:btz_pas_tarentin (ETT.tex:1358), SingularFlatAxioms.mem_Zplus

findings: Sbierski's and GKS's proofs use only a chronological past of the boundary point (sbierski2015c.txt:661; grant2018inextendibility.txt:427), and GKS's localising neighbourhoods give both sides; a chronological future serves equally, the case q not in O then using the openness of I-(q) instead of I+(q). This covers the BTZ points of E>=0-manifolds (rem:btz_pas_tarentin, ETT.tex:1358), where I- is empty; a model-free instance is closedHalfLine_oneSided.

labels.label: T-abs-locate-extension/3-ladder-form

source.statement: Q2 (locating an extension listed as purely causal or topological) and Q4 #2

hypotheses.paper: (SYNTHESIS Q2: locating an extension is purely causal or topological)
hypotheses.note: tarentin and causally_plain (ladder nodes beyond the target's uses), causally_arc_connected, M connected, O open non-empty and not dense (closure O != univ); no localisation hypothesis. Neither tarentin nor plainness can be dropped: tarentin_and_plain_needed (the lightlike line is arc-connected and tarentin, not plain; isolatedLine is arc-connected and plain, not tarentin; neither lets a chronal curve leave (0, oo), which is not dense; the two negations are themselves derived from the theorem).

findings: SYNTHESIS.md:50 lists 'locating an extension (some timelike curve leaves M)' among the purely causal or topological steps. In ETT it is so only with a localisation hypothesis (a chronal neighbour at some boundary point), or, with ladder nodes alone, for an image which is not dense, under tarentin and causal plainness.
questions: The dense case is open: do tarentin, causal plainness and causal arc-connectedness (possibly with push-up) give a chronal neighbour to some boundary point of a dense open set, e.g. M-tilde minus a point? By futureBoundary_union_pastBoundary_nonempty_iff this is the whole question; for dense O it amounts to excluding a point with I+ and I- empty. Reading taken: none; the theorem is stated for closure O != univ only.

labels.label: T-abs-locate-extension/4-density

hypotheses.paper: (Sbierski's proof works in an arbitrary small neighbourhood U of any boundary point, sbierski2015c.txt:661-671)
hypotheses.note: HasChronalNeighbour at the boundary points; C.CausallyArcConnected. Conclusion: every boundary point with a chronal neighbour is a limit of endpoints of leaving curves, each curve inside the given neighbourhood

findings: Implicit in Sbierski's proof (the curve stays in any small neighbourhood of any boundary point) and not stated by either source: the future and past boundaries are dense in the boundary of iota(M) when every boundary point has a chronal neighbour.

kb_proposals: Locating an extension is a characterisation, not a construction: under causal arc-connectedness a chronal curve leaves an open O iff some point of the boundary of O has a chronal neighbour (Causality.futureBoundary_union_pastBoundary_nonempty_iff), and a future one iff I+(O) is not contained in O (futureBoundary_nonempty_iff); the first exit is ChronalCurveOn.exists_firstExit (T-abs-locate-extension).

A cheap local, plain, causally open, arc-connected line with a chronologically isolated point: Causal.isolatedLine (the timelike line of R minus {0}, 0 related to itself only). It refutes any claim that plainness, causal openness or arc-connectedness give chronology at every point (T-abs-locate-extension).

The lightlike line is causally arc-connected and tarentin (lightlikeLine_causallyArcConnected; lightlikeLine_tarentin := timelikeLine_tarentin, by defeq: the two lines have the same causal relation) (T-abs-locate-extension).

A model-free arc-connected point with I- empty and I+ non-empty (a BTZ-like point without E0): the endpoint of Causal.closedHalfLine on Ici (0 : R); its relations are written with 'every point between x and y lies in U', converted to an interval of R by closedHalfLine_between_iff (T-abs-locate-extension).

Under causal arc-connectedness p in Z+ iff I+(p) is non-empty with no separation axiom (Causality.CausallyArcConnected.mem_Zplus_iff); the library's AbsolutelyMinimal.mem_Zplus_iff asks T1 (T-abs-locate-extension).
